topic.title: Model and prompt registry — versioning, approval and rollback

outcomes: Design immutable model and prompt versions with provenance and content digests.
Separate experiment tracking, artifact storage, model registry and prompt registry responsibilities.
Promote candidates through policy gates, human approval and compatibility checks.
Manage aliases such as candidate, staging, production and champion without mutating versions.
Build atomic release bundles that bind model, prompt, tokenizer, tool schema and evaluation report.
Rollback by moving aliases to a known-good version while preserving complete audit history.
prerequisites: Model artifacts, prompt templates, evaluation metrics, Git and CI/CD basics

glossary.definition: A governed catalog of immutable model versions, provenance, metadata and deployment aliases.
A versioned catalog of prompt templates, variable schemas, model compatibility and evaluation evidence.
A cryptographic hash identifying exact model or prompt bytes.
A mutable pointer such as staging or production that resolves to one immutable version.
A controlled alias update after required automated and human gates pass.
A compatible, immutable set of model, prompt, tokenizer, tool schema, configuration and evaluation artifacts.
Evidence linking a release to source run, dataset, code commit, build and evaluation.
Moving an alias back to a previously approved immutable version, not editing the current version.
The declared input/output schema and constraints for a model artifact.
A lifecycle state that blocks new use while preserving existing references and audit history.

explanation.problem: A model file in object storage is not a release process. Teams need to know exactly which weights, prompt, tokenizer, tool schema, configuration and evaluation report are running in production. They must prevent unreviewed changes, promote compatible candidates and recover quickly without overwriting history.
explanation.plainLanguage:
Experiment tracking answers how a model was trained. Artifact storage holds the bytes. A model registry governs named model versions, provenance, signatures, tags, approval and deployment aliases. A prompt registry does the same for prompt templates and their variable schemas. Keep these responsibilities separate so a training run does not automatically become a production release.

Treat every model version as immutable. Record model name, semantic or monotonic version, artifact URI, SHA-256 digest, source run ID, code commit, dataset snapshot, framework/runtime, input/output signature, license, security scan and evaluation report. If weights change, register a new version. Never replace bytes behind an existing version number.

Prompt versions also need immutable identity. Record template bytes/hash, prompt variables and types, system/developer/user message structure, model compatibility, tool schema versions, safety policy version, token budget, owner and evaluation results. A one-word prompt edit can change behavior; create a new prompt version and rerun the evaluation suite.

Aliases are mutable pointers to immutable versions. Typical aliases include candidate, staging, production and champion. Deployments resolve an alias at startup or through a controlled refresh mechanism. Store alias history with who changed it, when, why and the previous target. Avoid hard-coding a version in many services or changing the artifact behind an alias invisibly.

Promotion is a policy decision. A candidate may require evaluation thresholds, safety checks, artifact integrity, provenance completeness, compatibility tests, vulnerability scans, cost/latency limits and human approval. A passed accuracy score alone is insufficient. A model with better quality but incompatible tokenizer or tool schema must not be promoted.

Build a release bundle to prevent model/prompt drift. Bind the model digest, prompt version, tokenizer version, inference configuration, tool schemas, retrieval index contract, safety policy and evaluation report into one canonical manifest. Hash and sign the manifest. The serving system verifies the bundle before loading it.

Model compatibility is more than architecture name. Check framework/runtime version, tokenizer vocabulary, input schema, output schema, quantization format, hardware requirements, embedding dimension, tool schema and prompt variable contract. A prompt can reference a tool that the deployed agent does not expose; a model can emit a different JSON schema than the API expects.

Rollback should be fast and non-destructive. Move production alias to the previous known-good release bundle, verify health and keep the failed version for analysis. Do not delete or rewrite it. If the old model requires a matching prompt or tokenizer, roll back the complete bundle rather than only the weights.

Registry permissions should be role-based. Researchers can register candidates; evaluators can attach results; reviewers can approve; release managers can move production aliases; services can resolve approved aliases. Separate approval from promotion when the same person should not self-approve a high-impact release.

Lifecycle management includes candidate, approved, staging, production, deprecated, archived and quarantined states. Quarantine versions with compromised provenance or security findings. Deprecation should block new deployments but preserve running references until migration completes. Retention and deletion must respect legal, privacy and reproducibility requirements.

Connect the registry to CI/CD. A build creates a candidate, signs and stores its artifacts, runs evaluation, attaches evidence, requests approval, promotes staging, performs smoke/canary checks and finally moves production alias. Every step is idempotent and auditable. Deployment strategies are covered separately; this topic focuses on release identity and governance.
explanation.mentalModel: Register immutable artifacts → verify provenance/signatures/compatibility → evaluate → approve → create release bundle → move alias → verify → rollback alias if needed.
limitations: A registry does not guarantee model quality; evaluation and production monitoring are separate controls.
Aliases are mutable and require audit, cache invalidation and atomic update semantics.
Model and prompt compatibility must be tested as a bundle, not inferred from matching names.
Artifact hashes verify integrity, not trust; signatures and provenance validation are also needed.
Rollback may require compatible runtime, tokenizer, schema and infrastructure still being available.
Registry state alone cannot prove which version a serving process loaded; runtime attestation/telemetry is required.
explanation.everydayAnalogy: A pharmacy keeps each medicine batch sealed and numbered. A pharmacist checks the batch, expiry, prescription and approval before placing it on the shelf. If a batch is recalled, the shelf label is moved back to a previous approved batch; the original batch record is never rewritten.
explanation.mathMadeSimple: Production alias points to model v12 + prompt v8. A candidate v13 + prompt v9 passes quality gates but fails tool-schema compatibility. Promotion must stop. After compatibility is fixed, a new release bundle is created and production alias moves atomically. If canary errors rise from 0.5% to 4%, rollback points to the previous bundle without modifying v13.
explanation.productionImpact: Production registries require immutable artifact digests, signed release manifests, provenance, model signatures, prompt schemas, compatibility matrices, approval policy, atomic alias updates, rollback history, role separation and runtime version telemetry.

useCase.scenario: A team promotes a customer-support LLM update. The candidate model, prompt template, tokenizer, tool schemas and safety policy are packaged into one release bundle. CI attaches evaluation and security evidence; a reviewer approves staging; the release manager moves production alias after smoke tests.
constraints: Every release has complete provenance and verified digests.
Promotion requires independent evidence and authorized approval.
Alias updates are atomic and audited.
Rollback moves the full release bundle to a known-good target.
useCase.successMetric: Every serving instance can identify and verify the exact approved model/prompt release bundle, and rollback restores a compatible known-good bundle without losing history.

dataFlow.payload: artifact URI + digest + source run + signature

dataFlow.purpose: Load and attest exact release identity.

trustBoundaries: Only authorized roles can register, approve or promote versions.
Artifacts are immutable and verified by digest/signature before use.
Prompt templates and metadata are treated as code and reviewed for injection/secret risks.
Release bundles bind model, prompt, tools, tokenizer and policy versions.
Serving runtime resolves approved aliases and emits loaded version/digest telemetry.
failurePaths: Artifact digest mismatch: quarantine version and block promotion.
Prompt variable/tool schema mismatch: compatibility gate fails.
Quality/safety gate fails: candidate cannot move to staging/production.
Unauthorized alias update: RBAC denies and records audit event.
Alias update race: compare-and-swap version prevents lost update.
Production regression: alias rolls back to previous compatible bundle.
Deprecated version still referenced: preserve runtime compatibility until migration completes.

workedExample.problem: Promote a candidate model and prompt, then roll back when canary errors rise.
workedExample.input: Current production bundle=release-12 (model v12, prompt p8). Candidate=model v13, prompt p9; quality=0.94; compatibility initially passes; reviewer approves.

steps.reasoning: Register model and prompt as immutable versions with source run, code commit and SHA-256 digests.
Bind model, prompt, tokenizer, tool schema, safety policy and evaluation report hashes.
Reviewer approves exact manifest H1; release manager atomically moves staging then production alias.
Canary error rate reaches 4%, exceeding the 1% threshold.
Move production alias to prior compatible release-12 and verify health; retain failed release for analysis.

workedExample.expectedOutput: Production resolves the previous approved bundle; no model or prompt version is overwritten and all promotion/rollback actions are audited.

implementations.expectedResult: Immutable model/prompt versions, compatibility gates, approval, release bundles, alias promotion and rollback.

failures.name: Mutable model version
failures.symptom: The same model version resolves to different weights over time.
failures.rootCause: Artifact bytes overwritten behind a stable version name.
failures.recovery: Immutable version plus content digest; register a new version for changed bytes.
failures.regressionTest: Re-register same name/version with different digest is rejected.

failures.name: Prompt/model incompatibility
failures.symptom: New prompt calls unavailable tools or sends wrong input schema.
failures.rootCause: Prompt and model/tool schemas promoted independently.
failures.recovery: Promote one release bundle with compatibility validation.
failures.regressionTest: Tool schema mismatch blocks bundle creation.

failures.name: Missing provenance
failures.symptom: Candidate cannot be traced to training data or code.
failures.rootCause: Registry accepts artifact without source run, dataset and commit metadata.
failures.regressionTest: Missing source run or dataset hash leaves candidate unpromotable.

failures.name: Self-approval
failures.symptom: Same actor registers and approves a high-impact production release.
failures.rootCause: No role separation or approval policy.
failures.recovery: Require independent authorized reviewer and release manager.
failures.regressionTest: Creator cannot approve own candidate under separation-of-duties policy.

failures.name: Alias race
failures.symptom: Concurrent release managers overwrite a newer production alias.
failures.rootCause: Alias update has no expected version/CAS check.
failures.regressionTest: Stale expected alias version is rejected.

failures.name: Unsafe rollback
failures.symptom: Model weights revert but prompt/tokenizer remain incompatible.
failures.rootCause: Rollback moves individual artifacts instead of whole release bundle.
failures.recovery: Rollback the full bundle and verify runtime compatibility.
failures.regressionTest: Rollback target must include all required bundle components.

failures.name: Unauthorized release manager
failures.symptom: A researcher or unrelated service moves the production alias.
failures.rootCause: Promotion and rollback accept an actor identity without checking a server-derived role allow-list.
failures.recovery: Derive role membership from authenticated server identity and enforce it inside the registry service.
failures.regressionTest: A non-release-manager actor is rejected for both promotion and rollback.

failures.name: Invalid evaluation score or missing evidence
failures.symptom: A malformed quality score or empty evaluation reference is accepted into a release bundle.
failures.rootCause: Bundle creation does not validate metric bounds or evidence identity.
failures.recovery: Require a non-empty immutable evaluation report hash and a normalized score between zero and one.
failures.regressionTest: Scores outside [0,1] and missing evaluation evidence are rejected.

guidedExercise.title: Promote an approved release bundle
guidedExercise.instructions: Move an alias only when quality, compatibility and approval all pass; retain previous alias history.
guidedExercise.solutionCode:
def can_promote(quality, compatible, approved, threshold=0.90):
    return quality >= threshold and compatible is True and approved is True
guidedExercise.unitTests:
assert can_promote(0.94, True, True)
assert not can_promote(0.89, True, True)
assert not can_promote(0.95, False, True)
assert not can_promote(0.95, True, False)

miniAppIntegration.projectGoal: Build a model/prompt registry console with immutable versions, release bundles, approvals and alias history.
steps: Register model and prompt versions with artifact/template digests.
Attach training run, dataset and evaluation provenance.
Validate model signature, prompt variables, tokenizer and tool schema.
Create release bundle manifest and calculate its digest.
Request reviewer approval bound to exact manifest hash.
Promote staging and production aliases using expected alias version.
Inject canary regression and roll back the full release bundle.
Inspect audit trail, deprecation state and runtime-resolved digest.

scenarioQuiz.question: What should happen when model weights change?
options: Register a new immutable version and digest
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Model versions are immutable; changed bytes require a new version and provenance.

scenarioQuiz.question: Why bundle model and prompt versions together?
options: To validate model, prompt, tokenizer and tool compatibility as one release
scenarioQuiz.explanation: The runtime contract spans model, prompt, tokenizer, tools and policy.

scenarioQuiz.question: What is the safest rollback operation?
options: Move production alias to previous approved release bundle
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Rollback moves the alias to a known-good compatible bundle while preserving history.

scenarioQuiz.question: Who should approve a high-impact release?
options: An authorized independent reviewer under separation of duties
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Independent approval and role separation prevent self-approval and unauthorized promotion.

rubric.evidence: Model/prompt versions include digests, source run, dataset and code lineage.
Model, prompt, tokenizer, tools and safety policy are bound and validated.
Atomic alias update, expected version and full-bundle rollback are tested.
Alias history and loaded release digest are observable.

evidence: Approval is bound to exact bundle manifest.
Rollback restores complete prior bundle and preserves audit history.

codeWalkthrough.lines: if actor not in server_derived_release_manager_roles: deny()
codeWalkthrough.explanation: The registry must enforce authorization at the write boundary; a client-provided role or UI toggle is not an authorization source.
A version points to immutable bytes and a content digest.

codeWalkthrough.lines: release = {model, prompt, tokenizer, tools, policy, eval}
codeWalkthrough.explanation: The bundle captures the complete serving contract, not only weights.
Approval authorizes the exact release manifest that was reviewed.
Rollback changes the pointer and preserves all version and audit history.
Normalize evaluation scores and bind the exact evaluation evidence into the release manifest before approval.
